algorithms.name: Uniform sampling A_u (static proportions with omega = 1/K)

bound.regime: T -> infinity, to first order in the exponent

symbols.Gamma_omega: inf over lambda in Alt(mu) of sum_k omega_k KL(lambda_k, mu_k)
symbols.omega: static allocation vector with all entries positive

conditions: omega in the interior of the simplex
tuning: sampling counts satisfy |N_{T,k} - T omega_k| <= K

source.label: thm:oracle_difficulty_sp
source.quote: Let $\mathcal A_\omega^{sp}$ be a static proportions algorithm parametrized by $\omega \in \triangle_K^0$. For all $\mu \in \mathcal D$, $\lim_{T \to +\infty}h_{\mu, T}(\mathcal A^{sp}_\omega) = \Big(\inf_{\lambda \in \alt(\mu)} \sum_{k} \omega_k \KL(\lambda_k, \mu_k) \Big)^{-1}$.

results.notes: This is an exact limit, so it is also a matching lower bound; I recorded it once as an upper bound. Since h = T/log(1/p), it means p = exp(-T*Gamma_omega*(1+o(1))). The paper says it is adapted from Glynn & Juneja (2004), so is_new is false.

symbols.omega_min: smallest entry of the allocation vector omega

conditions: Quantity is the maximal difficulty ratio sup_lambda limsup_T T/(H_{C^sp}(lambda) log(1/p_{lambda,T})), measured relative to the oracle static-proportions difficulty
tuning: omega in the interior of the simplex

source.label: thm:uniform_upper_bound
source.quote: For all $\omega \in \triangle_K^0$, the static proportions algorithm $\mathcal A_\omega^{sp}$ belongs to $\overline{\mathcal C^{sp}}$ and satisfies $\sup_{\lambda\in \mathcal D} R_{H_{\mathcal C^{sp}}, \infty}(\mathcal A_\omega^{sp}, \lambda) \le (\min_{j \in [K]} \omega_j)^{-1}$.

results.notes: This is the general form for any allocation omega; the uniform-sampling case is recorded separately as r3.

conditions: Quantity is the maximal difficulty ratio relative to the oracle static-proportions difficulty H_{C^sp}

source.label: thm:uniform_upper_bound
source.quote: In particular, for $A_u \in \mathcal C^{sp}$ the uniform sampling algorithm (static proportions with proportion $1/K$ for all arms), $\sup_{\lambda\in \mathcal D} R_{H_{\mathcal C^{sp}}, \infty}(\mathcal A_u, \lambda) \le K$.

bound.expression_latex: \inf_{\mathcal A \in \mathcal C_\infty} \sup_{\lambda \in \mathcal D}  R_{H_{\mathcal C^{sp}}, \infty}(\mathcal A, \lambda) = K

conditions: Quantity is the maximal difficulty ratio relative to H_{C^sp}

source.label: thm:positivity_LB
source.quote: On the Positivity problem, where we check whether there is an arm with mean lower than a threshold $\theta$, $\inf_{\mathcal A \in \mathcal C_\infty} \sup_{\lambda \in \mathcal D}  R_{H_{\mathcal C^{sp}}, \infty}(\mathcal A, \lambda) = K$.

results.notes: The theorem states an equality. The matching upper bound comes from uniform sampling (Theorem 5, r3). The proof lets the alternative mean go to the lower end of the exponential family's mean range.

bound.expression_latex: \inf_{\mathcal A \in \mathcal C_\infty} \sup_{\lambda \in \mathcal D} R_{H_{\mathcal C^{sp}}, \infty}(\mathcal A, \lambda) \ge 1

conditions: Quantity is the maximal difficulty ratio relative to H_{C^sp}
there is an L2 ball centred at eta in cl(D) in which i* takes two values separated by a hyperplane through eta
Gaussian arms with known (possibly different) variances

source.label: thm:flat_boundary
source.quote: Suppose that there is an $L^2$ ball $B(\eta, r)$ with center $\eta \in \mathrm{cl}(\mathcal D)$ and radius $r > 0$ such that $i^\star$ takes only two values in $B(\eta, r)$ ... Then for Gaussian arms (each with a known but possibly different variance), the lowest maximal difficulty ratio is $\inf_{\mathcal A \in \mathcal C_\infty} \sup_{\lambda \in \mathcal D} R_{H_{\mathcal C^{sp}}, \infty}(\mathcal A, \lambda) \ge 1$.

results.notes: Lemma 16 states the same bound for Gaussian half-space identification as a special case, so I did not record it separately.

bound.expression_latex: \inf_{\mathcal A \in \mathcal C_\infty} \sup_{\lambda \in \mathcal D} R_{H_{\mathcal C},\infty}(\mathcal A, \lambda) \ge (3/80)\log(K)

conditions: Quantity is the maximal difficulty ratio relative to H_C, the oracle difficulty of any algorithm class C that contains the static proportions algorithms

source.label: thm:gaussian_bai_no_complexity
source.quote: Consider the BAI task with Gaussian distributions with variance 1. For any class $\mathcal C$ containing the static proportions algorithms, $\inf_{\mathcal A \in \mathcal C_\infty} \sup_{\lambda \in \mathcal D} R_{H_{\mathcal C},\infty}(\mathcal A, \lambda) \ge (3/80)\log(K)$ .

results.notes: The infimum is over all algorithm families. The paper remarks that the bound extends to c*log(K) for other exponential families with means in a bounded interval.

bound.expression_latex: \inf_{\mathcal A \in \mathcal C_\infty} \sup_{\lambda \in \mathcal D} R_{H_{\mathcal C}, \infty}(\mathcal A, \lambda) > 1

conditions: Quantity is the maximal difficulty ratio relative to H_C, for any class C containing the static proportions algorithms

source.label: thm:bernoulli_bai_no_complexity
source.quote: In BAI for Bernoulli bandits with two arms, for any class $\mathcal C$ containing the static proportions algorithms, $\inf_{\mathcal A \in \mathcal C_\infty} \sup_{\lambda \in \mathcal D} R_{H_{\mathcal C}, \infty}(\mathcal A, \lambda) > 1$ .

results.notes: The inequality is strict (> 1); the schema cannot express this. The explicit bound in the proof tends to about 1.22 as x -> 0. Together with Theorem 5, the true value lies in (1, 2].
